classification.difficultyReason: Combine several inclusive linear inequalities and calculate the vertices of their common region.

answer.short: The closed triangular region with vertices $(0,0)$, $(0,6)$ and $(3,3)$, including its boundaries.
answer.worked:
Draw solid boundaries $y=x$, $x=0$ and $x+y=6$. Shade their common region: above $y=x$, right of the $y$-axis and below $x+y=6$.

For the intersection of the two sloping boundaries, substitute $y=x$:
$$\begin{align*}x+x&=6\\2x&=6\\x&=3\\y&=3\end{align*}$$
On $x=0$, the other vertices are $(0,0)$ and $(0,6)$. All three boundaries are included.

spec.description: Solid boundary lines and the shaded common triangular region.

answer.short: The closed triangular region with vertices $(0,0)$, $(3,6)$ and $(6,6)$, including its boundaries.
answer.worked:
Draw solid boundaries $y=x$, $y=2x$ and $y=6$. Shade above $y=x$ and below both $y=2x$ and $y=6$.

The sloping boundaries meet where:
$$\begin{align*}x&=2x\\x&=0\\y&=0\end{align*}$$
At $y=6$, the boundary $y=2x$ gives:
$$\begin{align*}2x&=6\\x&=3\end{align*}$$
At $y=6$, the boundary $y=x$ gives $x=6$. Thus the vertices are $(0,0)$, $(3,6)$ and $(6,6)$. All boundaries are included.

spec.description: Common triangular region between two sloping lines and the horizontal upper boundary.

answer.short: The closed quadrilateral with vertices $(0,0)$, $(0,1)$, $\left(\frac73,\frac{17}3\right)$ and $(8,0)$, including its boundaries.
answer.worked:
Draw solid boundaries $x=0$, $y=0$, $y=2x+1$ and $x+y=8$. Shade the first-quadrant region below both sloping boundaries.

Substitute $y=2x+1$ into $x+y=8$:
$$\begin{align*}x+(2x+1)&=8\\3x+1&=8\\3x&=7\\x&=\frac73\end{align*}$$
Then:
$$\begin{align*}y&=2\left(\frac73\right)+1\\y&=\frac{17}3\end{align*}$$
The remaining vertices on the axes are $(0,0)$, $(0,1)$ and $(8,0)$. All four boundaries are included.

spec.description: First-quadrant common region bounded by the axes and two sloping lines.
